slides.text: Before retiring into public library administration, Vincent had spent twenty-five years as Interpol's most elusive art thief. He had cracked subterranean Zurich vaults and bypassed thermal infrared grids in Monaco without leaving a single thumbprint. But this morning, a crime of unspeakable depravity occurred in the staff breakroom: someone had stolen his vintage 1984 seal-tight avocado-green Tupperware container containing six homemade crab rangoon. Vincent put down his date stamp and tied back his hair. The gloves were coming off.

By noon, Vincent had mapped out the faculty lounge using satellite schematics, disabled the smoke detectors with dental floss, and dusted the microwave handle for latent prints. His tactical suspect board narrowed the culprit down to three targets: Mr. Henderson from Reference, whose breath smelled suspiciously of sweet-and-sour glaze, and Mrs. Gable, who was suddenly wearing a bulky cardigan. Using an endoscopic snake camera through the HVAC vents, Vincent initiated full surveillance on refrigerator shelf number two.

At precisely 1:14 PM, Vincent dropped through the acoustic ceiling tiles like a panther, landing in a combat crouch before the refrigerator. Cornered with the avocado lid midway to his mouth was none other than the Deputy Director of the County Library Board. Vincent clicked on a mini Maglite, illuminating the crumbs on the man’s lapel. 'Drop the rangoon, Harold,' Vincent whispered with icy serenity, 'or the Board hears about the overdue fine on your 1997 encyclopedia.'
